pr.title: gh-140067: Fix memory leak in sub-interpreter creation
pr.body:
This patch fixes a memory leak detected by AddressSanitizer during subinterpreter creation.
The original allocation pointer is now stored before the aligned memory block, removing
the need for the _malloced field in PyInterpreterState.

Thanks to @kumaraditya303 for highlighting the pointer overwrite issue.

Fixes #140067


<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-140067 -->
* Issue: gh-140067
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

auto_merge.commit_title: gh-140067: Fix memory leak in sub-interpreter creation  (#140111)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Fix memory leak in sub-interpreter creation caused by overwriting of the previously used `_malloced` field. Now the pointer is stored in the first word of the memory block to avoid it being overwritten accidentally. 

Co-authored-by: Kumar Aditya <kumaraditya@python.org>

I'm pretty sure this will break the ABI, so if we want to backport this to <3.15, we have to keep this field. It's fine to remove it for the main branch though.
Yes, I'll manually backport it keeping that field.
@kumaraditya303 maybe I should go with my original version?
No, this version is better. I'll handle the backport.

Or maybe create a new PR with changes for <3.15
